passageHtml:
Posted by the Student Services Office

12 April 2026

After-School Study Space Survey

Last month, 78% of the students who use after-school study spaces answered our survey. We consider this response rate high enough to reveal useful trends, although it does not represent every student.

The library remained the most popular location: 84% of respondents said it was quiet enough for individual work, up six percentage points from the previous survey. Satisfaction with available seats, however, fell from 71% to 58%. The cafeteria received the highest score for group discussion, but only 39% of respondents considered it suitable for concentrated reading.

From May, the library will add twenty movable chairs and keep the second floor open until 6:30 p.m. The cafeteria will introduce a quiet zone near the windows from 4:00 to 5:00 p.m. Cold drinks will still be allowed there, but hot meals must be eaten in the central dining area.

SpaceQuiet enoughEnough seatsGood for group work
Library84%58%31%
Cafeteria39%76%88%
Learning Commons67%64%72%

Student Comments

Riku: I usually work alone, so the library suits me. I sometimes arrive after club practice and cannot find a seat. Extending the second-floor hours should help.

Sofia: My project team meets in the cafeteria. We can talk freely, but music from the kitchen area makes serious reading difficult. The new quiet zone sounds useful, provided groups respect it.

How to Read the Results

The office warns that percentages should be compared carefully. A high score for one purpose does not mean a space is best for every purpose. For example, the cafeteria's strong group-work score reflects freedom to talk, while its lower quietness score reflects the same feature. Students were also allowed to select more than one space, so the figures should not be added together as if they represented separate groups.

The office will repeat the survey after the new seating and quiet-zone trial has operated for one term. Students will then be asked whether the changes improved their actual study experience, not merely whether they noticed them.

questions.question: Which option best describes the office's view of the survey?
options: The results are useless because not all students replied.
The response rate is sufficient to show meaningful patterns.
The survey proves that every student prefers the library.
The office plans to conduct the survey every month.
questions.answer: The response rate is sufficient to show meaningful patterns.
questions.evidence: high enough to reveal useful trends
questions.reason_ja: 十分な回答率で傾向を示せるという立場です。

questions.question: Which statement is true according to the report?
options: The cafeteria was rated best for silent reading.
The library received a higher quietness rating than before.
Hot meals will be allowed in the cafeteria quiet zone.
questions.answer: The library received a higher quietness rating than before.
questions.evidence: up six percentage points from the previous survey
questions.reason_ja: 図書館が静かだという評価は前回より6ポイント上昇しました。

questions.question: Which option best reflects Riku's comment?
options: He wants the library to close earlier.
He expects the announced change to solve a problem he faces.
He prefers group work in the cafeteria.
He thinks movable chairs will make the library noisier.
questions.answer: He expects the announced change to solve a problem he faces.
questions.evidence: Extending the second-floor hours should help.
questions.reason_ja: 部活動後に席がない問題が、開館時間延長で改善すると考えています。

questions.question: What concern does Sofia express?
options: Students may not follow the purpose of the quiet zone.
The cafeteria will stop allowing all drinks.
The library does not permit group projects.
The learning commons has too few seats.
questions.answer: Students may not follow the purpose of the quiet zone.
questions.reason_ja: 静かな区域を利用者が守ることが条件だと述べています。
